Subject: Streaming chat p99 regressions during evening peak — urgent

Hi Mina / Marissa,

We're seeing significant tail-latency regressions on the hosted streaming chat endpoint during our EMEA evening peak (~17:30–19:30 CET). Today at 18:02 we had p95 jump from ~300ms to ~1.8s and p99 spiking to 6–8s. Error rate for SSE connections rose from 1.2% to ~11% for a ~45 minute window; a few customer sessions dropped completely.

This is impacting our user experience on the GlowSign hosted chat widget (region: eu-west-1). We attach a short client trace (client-trace-20261122.log) showing request ids and timestamps. Key observations from our side: 
- Problem appears at ~18:00 CET and resolves around ~18:45 CET, but recurred briefly at 19:10 CET.
- Affected routes: /v1/stream/chat (SSE) behind the standard model config.
- No config changes on our end — we only saw a traffic pattern increase (~2x typical peak) during a marketing push.

Please advise next steps and whether Redwood has visibility into server-side backpressure or batching issues. This is customer-visible and we need an update within 30 minutes.

Thanks,
Elena Rossi
Head of Product Operations
GlowSign

Thanks, Mina / Elena — I've started pulling traces. Preliminary findings from a 17:50 CET sample window:

Hypothesis (initial): a combination of KV-cache churn and autoscaler reaction latency during a burst of long-lived streaming connections. Observed patterns:
- Batching queues for SSE connections showed sustained queue depth spikes (higher wait before token emission) for ~5–10s intervals.
- Several worker processes reported elevated GC/CPU stalls coincident with influx; kernel-level scheduling indicates short-lived thrash on a small subset of hosts.
- Autoscaler created new pods, but the new pods were not immediately attached to the streaming router due to a slow health-check path for long-lived sockets (we're seeing ~12–20s delay before new workers accept streams).

Immediate asks for GlowSign: can you surface 2–3 request ids from the trace around 18:02 CET that we can tie to server logs? If you can't, we can instrument an X-RI-Debug header to capture a richer server-side trace for a short window.

Mitigation suggestions (short term):
1) Temporarily shift GlowSign streaming traffic to the lower-latency fallback model (same semantics) for 30–60 minutes while we stabilize (we can route via policy).
2) Increase dedicated burst capacity for your account in eu-west-1 for the next 2 hours to absorb peak connection bursts.
3) Apply a quick change in the health-check path to mark new streaming workers as healthy faster (will take ~20–30 mins to roll).

I attached our collected server trace bundle for the window I pulled (sse-trace-20261122.zip).

I'll continue digging into kernel traces and GC profiles; will update in 15 minutes.

- Dev
Staff Software Engineer, Inference Runtime

Elena / team — thank you for your patience and for working through the call last night. Summary and immediate actions we executed overnight: 

1) Short-term mitigation (completed 18:55 CET): We routed GlowSign's streaming traffic to a verified lower-latency fallback model in eu-west-1. This reduced p99 from ~6–8s to ~700–900ms for the subsequent 90-minute window.
2) Burst capacity (completed 19:10 CET): We provisioned additional reserved burst capacity tied to your account to smooth the connection spike.
3) Rolling health-check fix (in progress): engineering pushed a health-check update to reduce worker warm-up recognition; full rollout target: 20:00 CET on 23 Nov.
4) Compensation proposal: Marissa proposed a 15% credit for the impacted billing period; we'll confirm the formal SLA mapping once GlowSign confirms the exact disconnect counts.

Next steps / timeline:
- Immediate: Dev will continue log-level analysis and deliver a root-cause hypothesis within 6 hours.
- 14:00 CET 23 Nov: Postmortem call (we've invited Elena + engineering + CS).
- Deliverable: 48-hour postmortem doc with action items, RCA, and mitigation plan.
